items.q: Is Arabic Era actually free to use?
items.a: Yes. Browsing universities, comparing programmes, and getting consultation from our counsellors is free for students. We work with universities and don't charge students for guidance.

items.q: How accurate and up to date is your fee and requirement data?
items.a: We compile programme data from official university sources and recognised education portals, cross-checking where possible. Fees and requirements change yearly, so we always recommend confirming final figures directly with the university before you apply.

items.q: Do you help with the actual application, not just comparisons?
items.a: Yes. Beyond browsing, our counsellors help with shortlisting, document preparation, and application submission. Book a free consultation and we'll walk you through it.

items.q: Do you only cover public universities, or private ones too?
items.a: Both. Our directory includes public universities, private universities, and private university colleges across Malaysia, so you can compare across all of them in one place.

story.label: Our story
story.title: A single place for every option.
story.p1: Arabic Era was created to simplify the university search and application process for students in Malaysia. We noticed that finding the right program — with accurate fees, requirements, and accreditation info — was unnecessarily difficult.
story.p2: Our platform aggregates data from official university sources and recognized education portals, giving students a single place to compare options and make informed decisions.
story.p3: Beyond the website, we offer free consultation services to guide students through the application and enrollment process.

descriptions.business-administration: Business administration covers how organisations are run — strategy, operations, marketing, finance, and people. It is one of the broadest degrees in Malaysia and leads into management, banking, consulting, and entrepreneurship.
descriptions.accounting: Accounting teaches financial reporting, auditing, taxation, and business law, and is the standard route toward professional qualifications such as ACCA, CPA, and CIMA.
descriptions.computer-science: Computer science is the study of algorithms, software, and computing systems. Programmes cover programming, data structures, databases, and networks, with specialisations such as AI and cybersecurity.
descriptions.information-technology: Information technology focuses on applying computing systems inside real organisations — networks, databases, cloud infrastructure, and IT operations — rather than on the theory of computation.
descriptions.software-engineering: Software engineering applies engineering principles to building and maintaining software across the full lifecycle: requirements, design, development, testing, and delivery.
descriptions.cyber-security: Cybersecurity prepares graduates to protect systems and data, covering network defence, ethical hacking, cryptography, digital forensics, and security governance.
descriptions.artificial-intelligence: Artificial intelligence covers machine learning, neural networks, natural language processing, and robotics, and how these techniques are applied in products and research.
descriptions.education: Education programmes prepare teachers and trainers, combining pedagogy and child development with classroom practice and supervised teaching placements.
descriptions.business: General business degrees give a broad foundation across marketing, finance, management, and operations, and let students specialise later.
descriptions.mechanical-engineering: Mechanical engineering deals with machines, materials, and energy — from design and thermodynamics to manufacturing, automation, and robotics.
descriptions.management: Management degrees focus on leading teams and organisations: strategy, organisational behaviour, operations, and decision-making.
descriptions.communication: Communication programmes cover media, journalism, public relations, and digital content, blending theory with practical production skills.
descriptions.psychology: Psychology studies the mind and behaviour, covering developmental, cognitive, social, and clinical psychology, with routes into counselling and human resources.
descriptions.nursing: Nursing prepares registered nurses through clinical training in patient care, anatomy, pharmacology, and community health.
descriptions.finance: Finance covers financial markets, investments, corporate finance, and risk management, usually with strong quantitative and analytical training.
descriptions.civil-engineering: Civil engineering designs and builds infrastructure — structures, roads, bridges, and water systems — with strong foundations in mechanics and materials.
descriptions.law: Law programmes cover constitutional, contract, criminal, and commercial law, preparing graduates for legal practice, corporate, and compliance careers.
descriptions.architecture: Architecture combines design studio work with building technology, history, and environmental design, leading toward professional architectural practice.
descriptions.pharmacy: Pharmacy covers drug science, pharmacology, and patient care, preparing graduates for hospitals, community pharmacies, and the pharmaceutical industry.
descriptions.tourism-management: Tourism and hospitality management covers hotel and event operations, travel services, and destination marketing.
